# 08 diff-review — panel seating, CI/hook, telemetry

**Verdict: ACCEPT**, with minor findings only.

**Q1. Seats.** Required entries are always seated (`pinned_seats`, `panel/plan.rs:832`, `routing.rs:822`); `k` is never cut below the pin count (`lab_seat_cap` counts pins + unheld labs, `routing.rs:946`). A lab-count cut is warned (`plan.rs:897-905`), two required of one lab too (`plan.rs:929-936`). Two gaps: (a) the weighty guarantee is skipped with no warning when the only eligible weighty entry shares a lab with a required non-weighty entry — `tier_owed` is true but the tier pool is empty (`plan.rs:782-790`, `routing.rs:757-775`) → finding #3; (b) a lab held by its reserve simply leaves the eligible set; the "panel size reduced" line covers that.

**Q2. Labs/records.** MiniMax and Meta-Llama exist in the class/OpenRouter tables but not in `LAB_VENDORS`, so an endpoint entry on `api.minimax.io` is lab `minimax` while a codex `minimax-m3` (or `meta-llama/...`) entry is a singleton: two entries of one maker can be seated → finding #4. Other claude endpoint hosts fall back to the model prefix, which is right for every family the roster uses. `ext.c3.seating` is written only when `labs_shared || tier_seated` (`plan.rs:980-989`), and replay reproduces those seats (test). But `c3 router explain` marks a seat-taker without checking availability/refusal/context → finding #2. The CHANGELOG's "a file the user rewrote is never edited" is only a title-line test → finding #6.

**Q3. CI check.** gh is killed at 3 s/10 s (`ci_check.rs:144-193`), the hook's 5 s wrapper returns without waiting (`hook/mod.rs:86-119`), nothing writes outside `<codex home>/c3`, no non-gh process is run, no child, never a refusal; cancelled/skipped decide nothing. Two real defects: a run title is forwarded verbatim — `one_line` collapses only whitespace, so ESC/BEL/NUL and instructions reach the session (#1); and `default_branch` can fall back to local `main` when `origin/HEAD` names a remote-only default, so the check can describe a non-default branch (#7). Also `remotes_name_github` matches a non-GitHub URL whose path contains `github.com/` (#8), the wording says "latest run" for the latest *completed* run (#10), and two sessions can both call gh / lose one attempt (benign, read-modify-write with atomic rename).

**Q4. Hook scripts.** Order, once-only, 400-char cut, 10-line cap and fallback are implemented and tested. Two divergences: a >400-char non-ASCII line is cut at 400 UTF-16 units in the `.ps1` (can split a surrogate pair) versus characters in awk, so "byte-identical" fails off ASCII, and the `.ps1` catch path prints no waiting rule (#9). The 10-line cap can silently drop the CI line last (#9). A non-ASCII cut is already known.

**Q5. File ops.** `repair_delegation_rule` reuses `edit_refusal`/`replace_file` (temp+rename, link and hard-link refusal, snapshot re-read, original line endings kept) — no write outside the target. The kimi removal refuses a link root before any unlink and runs no git command after any error (`kimi.rs:2741-2768`); the junction/sentinel and injected-failure tests match. Residual race: a link created after the sweep and before `git worktree remove`.

**Q6. Telemetry.** A name is sent only from `CLAUDE_MODELS` or a `(class, id)` published by the built-in catalog / a `"public": true` source; `[1m]` is stripped in any case; no vendor class → `other`; the Claude shape no longer authorises (`classes.rs:331-361`, `models.rs:758-783`). One leak path: trust is per source (host), not per URL, while `collect` keeps only the first catalog per host → finding #5.

**Q7. Untested:** the tier guarantee with a pinned same-lab entry; explain marks against unavailable entries; both hook scripts with long non-ASCII lines; the CI check against real `gh`; two catalogs on one host; a MiniMax/Meta-Llama roster; the 10-line cap.

## Requested checks
- RC1 (read-only, workspace-write for a scratch roster, ~5 min): roster with zhipu #2 available and #3 unavailable; run `c3 router explain --purpose framing` and `c3 consult --panel --dry-run`; the mark must not name a seat the dry run leaves empty.
- RC2 (workspace-write, ~10 min): config `model_catalogs: ["https://catalogs.example/v1/models", {"url":"https://catalogs.example/pub/v1/models","public":true}]` with the first listing `qwen/private-sauce`; serialize a backfill event for model `private-sauce`; expect `other`.
- RC3 (workspace-write, ~3 min): run both hook scripts with `c3: ` + 199 ASCII characters + 2 emoji; expect identical output and no lone surrogate.

findings.claim: The red-CI line forwards a workflow-run displayTitle into the session after one_line, which collapses whitespace only; ESC/BEL/NUL and arbitrary instructions survive, so a title a stranger controls can inject control sequences or instructions into every session start (once a day per repository).
findings.trigger: A failed run on the default branch whose displayTitle contains an ANSI escape or text addressed to the agent.

evidence.observation: The title goes through c3_core::one_line and a 100-char cut only.
one_line tests char::is_whitespace only; no other control character is removed.

findings.verification: Call failure_line with a displayTitle containing \u{1b}[2J and an instruction, print the result, and check the ESC byte survives.
findings.remedy: Strip C0/C1 control characters (keep printable text) in one_line or in the title, and consider quoting or labelling the title as untrusted.

findings.claim: c3 router explain decides which entry 'takes its seat' per lab from roster.active_entries() with only on-request, held and weighty checks; an entry skipped for unavailable auth, a context window or a refusal is still marked as its lab's pick and its siblings as kept out, so the table names seats the real panel would never fill.
findings.trigger: explain on a roster whose best-weighted entry of a lab is unavailable (missing key, too small a context window).

evidence.observation: lab_picks builds LabRow from active_entries; drawable = !on_request && !held && !(weighty&&!weighty_purpose); no member-election state is consulted.
run_explain computes no availability/refusal and appends the mark unconditionally at 403.

findings.verification: Give roster position 3 of one lab an unauthenticated endpoint and position 2 of the same lab a key; compare explain's mark with consult --panel --dry-run.
findings.remedy: Build the rows from the same member election the panel uses (providers panel_members), or mark the seat as conditional.

findings.claim: The upper-tier guarantee is silently skipped when the only eligible weighty entries share a lab with a required (non-weighty) entry: tier_owed is true, but open(seats, true) excludes every lab already held by a pin, so the pool is empty, no tier seat is drawn and no warning is emitted - although no required entry is weighty, which is the only exception the invariant allows.
findings.trigger: A roster with required #1 (kimi, non-weighty) and weighty #2 (kimi, same lab) on a weighty purpose with size >= 2.

evidence.observation: tier is every eligible weighty position; no same-lab check.
tier_owed ignores pins' labs; open(&seats,true) filters labs in seated_labs, so a same-lab pin empties the pool and the seat is skipped.

findings.verification: Unit-test select_panel_routing with required [1], weighty #2 of the same lab and purpose acceptance; assert a tier seat or a warning.
findings.remedy: When tier_owed is true and the tier pool is empty because of a pinned lab, treat the matching required entry as satisfying the guarantee and say so, or warn.

findings.claim: MiniMax and Meta-Llama are vendors in the class and OpenRouter tables but have no LAB_VENDORS prefix: an endpoint entry on api.minimax.io takes lab 'minimax' from lab_of_host, while a codex entry with minimax-m3, or an OpenRouter meta-llama id, becomes a singleton lab. Two entries of one maker are therefore seated together, contrary to the one-entry-per-lab rule.
findings.trigger: A roster with two MiniMax (or Meta-Llama) entries, one an endpoint entry with an empty lab and one a codex/OpenRouter id.

evidence.observation: LAB_VENDORS has no minimax, meta-llama or llama prefix.
lab_of_host returns 'minimax' for api.minimax.io/.cn.
The class table lists minimax and OPENROUTER_VENDORS maps 'minimax' to it.

findings.verification: Unit-test model_lab("minimax-m3") and model_lab("meta-llama/llama-4"), then select_panel_routing with an endpoint minimax entry and a codex one.
findings.remedy: Add minimax and meta-llama/llama prefixes to LAB_VENDORS so every class with a lab resolves to the same string.

findings.claim: Telemetry trust is keyed by the source name, which for a catalog is only the host, while collect fetches only the first catalog URL per host. If a private catalog is configured first on a host that also has a catalog declared "public": true, the state's ids come from the private URL and are still published (OpenRouter-style ids bind by slug regardless of the host's class).
findings.trigger: model_catalogs = ["https://catalogs.example/v1/models", {"url":"https://catalogs.example/pub/v1/models","public":true}] with the first listing e.g. qwen/private-sauce.

evidence.observation: catalog_source returns web:<host>, discarding the path.
collect skips a catalog whose source already occurred, so only the first URL per host is fetched.
published_from matches state sources to trusted sources by name; a <vendor>/<model> id binds by slug even when the host class is None.

findings.verification: Fixture with the two catalogs on one stub host and one alibaba-class reviewer with model private-sauce; serialize the backfill event and inspect details.model.
findings.remedy: Key trusted sources by the full URL and record the URL in the maintain state, or refuse two catalogs on one host with different public flags.

findings.claim: status_of calls a delegation rule C3-written whenever any line equals the template's title; doctor --fix then appends the section to a file the user rewrote around that title, although the CHANGELOG and README promise that a user-rewritten file is reported and never edited.
findings.trigger: .claude/rules/02-delegation.md that keeps C3's title line but has a user-written body and no BRANCHES section.

evidence.observation: template_title() is the first line; has_line compares any line; status_of derives c3_written from that single line.
with_branches_section appends for any c3_written file; repair_delegation_rule calls it unconditionally under --fix.

findings.verification: Run doctor --fix on a repo whose rule file is the title line plus 'my own rules', then diff the file.
findings.remedy: Require more evidence than the title (e.g. the template's next heading or a body hash), or change the documented rule to the title-line test.

findings.claim: The CI check asks gh for setup::branches::default_branch, which falls back to local main when origin/HEAD names a remote-only default (e.g. develop) and no local develop exists; the hook then reports the run of a branch that is not the repository's default and can miss a red default.
findings.trigger: A clone whose origin default is develop, with only a local main, and a red latest run on main.

evidence.observation: check() takes default_branch as the gh --branch value.
origin/HEAD is accepted only when the named branch exists locally, else main/master is used.

findings.verification: Scratch repo with origin/HEAD -> develop, no local develop and a local main; run the hook with a fake gh logging its --branch argument.
findings.remedy: Use the remote default name from origin/HEAD for the gh call even when no local branch exists, or state in the line that the branch is the local fallback.

findings.claim: remotes_name_github accepts any git remote output line containing "github.com/" or "github.com:", so a non-GitHub remote such as https://gitlab.example/github.com/mirror makes has_github_remote true; gh is started, fails, and the day's hook attempt is consumed.
findings.trigger: A remote URL whose path contains github.com/.

evidence.observation: remotes_name_github lower-cases the line and does a substring test; the unit test only covers a plain gitlab URL.

findings.remedy: Parse the remote URL/scp form and compare the host exactly with github.com.

findings.claim: The .ps1 cuts a long line at 400 UTF-16 code units (Substring can split a surrogate pair) while awk counts characters, so for a long non-ASCII line the two scripts print different text, contradicting the byte-identical claim; the .ps1 catch path also omits the waiting rule that the .sh always prints.
findings.trigger: A forwarded c3: line over 400 UTF-16 units with non-BMP characters, or an exception inside the .ps1.

evidence.observation: $t.Length/Substring(0,400) on UTF-16; catch prints only the error line.
awk length/substr counts characters (or bytes in a C locale) and the rule is always printed.

findings.verification: Run both scripts with "c3: " + 199 ASCII characters + 2 emoji and compare the outputs byte for byte.
findings.remedy: Cut on grapheme/text-element boundaries in PowerShell, and print the waiting rule in the catch block.

findings.claim: The printed sentence says 'the latest run on <branch> failed' although the value chosen is the latest completed, non-cancelled run; with a newer queued or in-progress run the sentence is literally untrue (the unit test encodes this behaviour).
findings.trigger: A failed completed run followed by a newer queued run on the same branch.

evidence.observation: runs are filtered to completed non-cancelled and sorted by createdAt; the message text does not say 'completed'.

findings.verification: Call failure_line with a failure at T1 and a queued run at T2>T1.
findings.remedy: Say 'the latest completed run' in the line, or state the run time.
